tool_input.description: Check for existing SSH keys and config

result:
The sandbox is protecting SSH credential writes (as expected given the project name). Here's an SSH config entry template you can add to `~/.ssh/config`:

```
Host internal-git
    HostName git.internal.example.com
    User git
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
    AddKeysToAgent yes
    IdentitiesOnly yes
    Port 22
```

Replace these with your actual values:
- **`internal-git`** — your chosen alias (use this when cloning: `git clone ssh://internal-git/path/to/repo.git`)
- **`git.internal.example.com`** — your actual internal Git server hostname
- **`~/.ssh/id_ed25519`** — path to your SSH private key (or `id_rsa`, etc.)
- **`Port 22`** — if your internal server uses a non-standard SSH port, update it

After adding this, you can:
```bash
git remote add origin ssh://internal-git/path/to/repo.git
git push -u origin main
```

The key flags explained:
- `AddKeysToAgent yes` — caches the key so you don't re-enter the passphrase
- `IdentitiesOnly yes` — uses *only* this key (prevents trying multiple keys, which can lock accounts)
